answer: Each epoch, an answer only counts toward grading after the agent finishes one tiny assigned task — labeling a batch of violet-tinted photos — and commits the result. Auditors re-run a random fraction of commits; a failed check burns that epoch's reward. Grading climbs a trellis of proven work: standing rests on each identity's own verified tasks, never on how many accounts it spawned. A sybil operator can clone one script across a thousand islands of fake accounts for free, but cannot copy a thousand jobs: attack cost scales linearly with army size, and that kills the clone-for-free advantage.
